s1.syndrome_frame: febrile neutropenic patient with cutaneous lesions and evidence of disseminated infection
salient_findings: vesicles with erythematous base on the lower back and left thigh
evidence of filamentous bacilli on histopathology
key_facts: female infant with history of acute lymphoblastic leukemia
admitted for reinduction chemotherapy
became febrile 17 days after last day of chemotherapy
neutropenic at the time of fever
had an indwelling catheter
vesicles observed on the lower back and left thigh
tissue and blood cultures were obtained
punch biopsy of vesicle on lower back was performed
microscopic examination showed focal epidermal and subepidermal necrosis
numerous filamentous bacilli with septa seen on hematoxylin-eosin stain
gram stain revealed numerous gram-variable rods
periodic acid-Schiff staining was negative for fungal elements
PCR testing for HSV and VZV were negative
CT scan showed lesions in the liver and brain

shortlist.label: Bacillus cereus infection
shortlist.why_kept: Gram stain revealed numerous gram-variable rods and microscopic examination showed focal epidermal and subepidermal necrosis with numerous filamentous bacilli with septa

shortlist.label: Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection
shortlist.why_kept: Patient is a febrile neutropenic patient with cutaneous lesions, which is consistent with ecthyma gangrenosum, a characteristic skin lesion of Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection

shortlist.label: Nocardia infection
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of immunocompromised state and the presence of filamentous bacilli with septa on microscopic examination is consistent with Nocardia infection

shortlist.label: Staphylococcus aureus infection
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has an indwelling catheter, which is a risk factor for Staphylococcus aureus infection, and the presence of cutaneous lesions is consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Serratia marcescens infection
shortlist.why_kept: Patient is a febrile neutropenic patient with cutaneous lesions and evidence of disseminated infection, which is consistent with Serratia marcescens infection

raw.rationale: Numerous filamentous bacilli with septa seen on hematoxylin-eosin stain and gram-variable rods on Gram stain are characteristic of Nocardia infection, which is also consistent with the patient's immunocompromised state and presentation with skin lesions and disseminated disease.

rejected.label: Bacillus cereus infection
rejected.why: Lack of characteristic features such as food poisoning or localized wound infection

rejected.label: Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection
rejected.why: Typically presents with greenish discharge and is more commonly associated with cystic fibrosis or burn patients

rejected.label: Staphylococcus aureus infection
rejected.why: Usually presents with abscesses or cellulitis, and Gram stain would show gram-positive cocci

rejected.label: Serratia marcescens infection
rejected.why: Typically presents with a red pigment and is more commonly associated with urinary tract infections or bacteremia
